questions.q: Why does rejection hurt so much, according to Jiang?
a: We blame it on ourselves rather than on circumstances
It threatens our basic survival needs today
Strangers are usually cruel by nature
It happens far more often than we expect
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a direct no is hard to pin on the environment, so it feels like a verdict on you.

questions.q: What does the summary mean by rejection has a number?
a: Enough attempts, with changed factors, will produce a yes
Every rejection can be scored on a ten-point scale
A fixed number of rejections is unavoidable
Only a set number of people will ever agree
questions.why: Lesson 2 says persistence and changing variables move you past that count toward a yes.

questions.q: Which examples does the summary give of ideas once laughed at?
a: Galileo's sun-centred model and Apple's early tablet
The telephone and the first airplane
Penicillin and the printing press
The internet and the smartphone
questions.why: Lesson 3 names Galileo, an early Apple tablet and Twitter's character limit as rejected first.

questions.q: What surprised Jiang about his rejection challenge?
a: How often people said yes when he simply asked
How rarely people responded to him at all
How quickly he became famous online
How much money the videos earned
questions.why: The review notes he was struck by how many things he obtained merely by asking.

questions.q: How does the summary say optimists view negative events?
a: As temporary, specific and impersonal
As proof that effort is wasted
As a test of personal character
As permanent lessons to remember
questions.why: Lesson 2 says seeing rejection as temporary, specific and impersonal changes your perspective.
